rationale: The expression is internally consistent and the lead-lag timing (financing first, accrual deterioration after) is a genuinely different mechanism from the archive's contemporaneous and delta×delta composites, though both legs are individually well-known anomalies and the closest archive analog (Industry AccrualFunding Shock) failed badly.

This is effectively the accrual × net-external-financing composite already tested repeatedly in the archive (DebtAdjusted CurrentAccrual Issuer, ProfitableAccrual EquityIssuer, EquityForDebt Accrual Recap), with the only change being a MIN over the two issuance legs — a cosmetic aggregation variant rather than a new mechanism.

Signs are coherent and substituting the working-capital component for total accruals in the archive's strongest performer (DebtIssue EarningsShortfall AccrualStress, t=-3.67) is a defensible decomposition, though the (dltis-dltr-ib)/at leg partly proxies low profitability and so risks reproducing a known profitability effect rather than a financing interaction.

Economically coherent as a debt-financed-buyback-with-soft-earnings story and not a duplicate of any archive entry, but the share-shrink leg pulls against the well-documented net-share-issuance/repurchase anomaly, so a weak or wrong-signed result is likely and the interaction must dominate a known main effect.

This is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested and weak archive signals (EquityForDebt Accrual Recap, t=-1.49; EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build, alpha ≈ 0) with no new economic content beyond swapping the accrual leg for the working-capital leg.

Little more than the sign-flipped accruals anomaly multiplied by the external-financing anomaly, closely overlapping the archive's already-successful Clean Accrual Net Capital Return, with the only differentiation being a first-difference on the financing leg — a variant already shown weak in Industry AccrualFunding Shock.
